clue.text: Tallies the notches put in it

definitions.meaning: second meaning: cuts or notches, the marks once cut into a tally stick

explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is the tally stick of the first half: a tally was a stick notched to keep count, and those notches were called scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is both a running total and a cut line made with a blade, so the plural fits counts and notches alike.

clue.text: I've been given the bird and all because of a broken con-rod!

definitions.note: the bird speaks in the first person: the answer is the bird the speaker has been given

indicators.note: a broken engine part is smashed out of shape, so its letters are put back together differently

parts.note: a con-rod is an engine's connecting rod, taken as written without the hyphen

explanation.surface: A motorist complains of being jeered at, all because of an engine breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given the bird' is an idiom for being booed, which hides the real job of 'the bird': it names the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A condor is a very large vulture of the Andes and California, so it is a bird.

clue.text: I see Les right with some souvenirs

parts.note: the letter C sounds like the word see
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone notices that their friend Les has the right sort of keepsakes.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: the pieces are mixed with no word saying so. Taking C for 'see' is a common sound-based convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Relics are objects kept from the past as reminders, much as souvenirs are kept from a trip.

clue.text: A violent effort in wet weather by a little saint

parts.note: ST is the short form of saint

explanation.surface: Someone struggles hard through a downpour beside a small holy figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' puts the two pieces side by side; the little saint comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a great or excessive exertion, close to a violent effort.

clue.text: Isn't able to or is able to lead the singing?

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the person who does it

parts.note: can't means is not able to

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: is someone fit to lead the choir or not?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue sets 'isn't able' against 'is able', a playful contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantor is the official who leads the singing in a synagogue or church choir.

clue.text: This miss is put out by such doctrines

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed and set awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young lady is offended by certain teachings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman; it is only four letters to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Isms are distinctive doctrines or theories, the word taken from endings such as socialism.

clue.text: It's nothing more than a lake

definitions.meaning: first meaning: only, being no more than what is said
second meaning: a small lake or pond, chiefly in British place names

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds dismissive of a lake; the two halves are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means only or simply; as a noun it is an old word for a lake or pool.

clue.text: That's my star fern! Move it! Take it somewhere else

indicators.note: an order to move things about tells the solver to shift the letters of the plant's name into new places

explanation.surface: A gardener shoos someone away from a prized fern, telling them to carry it elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To transfer something is to carry or convey it from one place to another, a plain synonym of the instruction.

clue.text: He fishes in the corner — right?

parts.note: a corner is an angle where two lines meet
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone points out a man fishing over in the corner and asks for confirmation.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is a person who fishes with rod and line, so 'he fishes' describes him.

clue.text: Examined by Ted's alien companion

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
E.T. is the friendly alien of the 1982 Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Someone has been looked over by a friend of Ted's from another world.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: the letters of TED'S and E.T. are mixed together with no word saying so; 'alien' suggests strangeness, which is the best hint of the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tested and examined are both past forms meaning checked or put to the proof.

clue.text: It takes Lee to organise this kind of group

indicators.note: organising means putting into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Only someone called Lee can set up a certain sort of club.
explanation.definitionFit: An elite is a select group thought to be the best of a larger body.

clue.text: To top it all, the queen sees him drink ing a lot

definitions.note: a man who drinks a lot; the paper prints a space inside 'drinking'

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Worst of all, Her Majesty catches a man drinking heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: 'To' and 'it all' are padding around TOP. ER is a crossword convention for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is an old word for a habitual heavy drinker.

clue.text: Doctors, for example, have to deal with the unwanted

indicators.note: to have something is to hold it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Physicians, among others, must handle what nobody else wants.
explanation.walkthrough: DRS holds EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the worthless residue at the bottom, figuratively the least wanted part of anything.

clue.text: I'm afraid Olive has a false god!

indicators.note: the phrase is said to have, or hold, the answer within its run of letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: An apology: sorry, but Olive worships something she shouldn't.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'afraid' and 'Olive'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or object worshipped as a deity, which in religious language is a false god.

clue.text: No, sir! There's nothing in such a prayer

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: O is the figure nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A firm refusal, followed by the observation that a certain prayer is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: An old loose clue: the letters of NO SIR are mixed without a word saying so, then the nought goes inside before the final N.
explanation.definitionFit: Orison is an old literary word for a prayer, as in Hamlet's 'Nymph, in thy orisons'.

clue.text: No rag is to be played on this instrument!

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ban on ragtime music for a particular instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rag' is ragtime music, which makes 'played' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a keyboard instrument with pipes, a common example of an instrument.

clue.text: Unfit to keep a pet in?

explanation.surface: A question: is a place unsuitable for keeping an animal in?
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: the letters of PET and IN are mixed with no word to say so.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means unsuited or lacking skill, a synonym of unfit.

clue.text: Cora's going all out to obtain an award

indicators.note: going all out suggests wild effort and disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An actress named Cora tries her hardest to win a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is the Academy Award statuette given for film achievement.

clue.text: Give a little wave to Pip and get right with the French

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone waves to a friend called Pip and makes peace with the French.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: R and PIP are mixed with no word to say so, and LE, French for 'the', ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripple is to form small waves, as a breeze does on water, so it is to give a little wave.

clue.text: I agree, Cecil! You must identify your country

indicators.note: to identify is to pick something out, here from inside a run of the clue's words

parts.note: the letters run across 'agree' and the start of 'Cecil'

explanation.surface: Someone tells Cecil they agree, then asks him to name the nation he comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your country' only defines it if you are Greek; the definition takes the voice of the surface speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a nation in south-east Europe, an example of a country.

clue.text: A schemer gets to come forth from it

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the phrase in front, lying within its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of 'schemer' and the start of 'gets'

explanation.surface: A plotter manages to escape from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From it' does double work, ending the surface and pointing back at the words that hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come out into view, which is to come forth.

clue.text: They grow on one and go red in degrees

indicators.note: to go wrong or go wild is to change form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: BAs are Bachelor of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: Something that sprouts on a person and blushes by stages.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is the Bachelor of Arts degree, so 'degrees' gives BAS; the letters of RED are mixed in among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Beards are hair that grows on a man's face, so they grow on one.

clue.text: Most bowlers look for shady places

indicators.note: most of something is all but a part, so one letter is lost

parts.note: bowlers are players who bowl, or round hats

explanation.surface: Cricketers and lawn bowlers like to find shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, the letter dropped is L in the middle, not the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a leafy, shaded arbour or retreat in a garden.

clue.text: You are given a taste of what it's like to be called shrewd

explanation.surface: Someone is given a sample of being thought clever.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: U and TASTE are mixed with no word to say so; the rest is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means sharp and quick to see an advantage, a synonym of shrewd.

clue.text: Set out and went red in that barren spot

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A traveller set off and got sunburnt in a wasteland.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is an arid, barren region where little grows.

clue.text: This morning, Miss Derek, you're to go to the pulpit-that old one

parts.note: Bo Derek is the American actress of the film 10

explanation.surface: An instruction to the film star to go up to the pulpit this morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Bo Derek was a famous film actress around 1980, so 'Miss Derek' is Bo.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambo is a raised reading desk or pulpit in early Christian churches, hence an old one.

clue.text: You're in a rut, Ena! It's power you must seek

definitions.note: the answer is the power sought

indicators.note: being in a rut suggests being stuck in a mess, so the following letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Advice to a stuck woman called Ena: find some strength.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue with a vague definition: nature is the power of the natural world, as in 'Mother Nature'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature can mean the creative force that governs the physical world, a power people seek or return to.

clue.text: There's a lot to be said for such a voice

explanation.surface: Praise for a particular singing voice.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: the letters of A LOT are mixed with no word saying so.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto is a singing voice lower than soprano, the highest male or lowest female range.

clue.text: You return the hat and get into a state

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: a hat is headwear, the 'the' is padding

explanation.surface: Someone brings back a hat and ends up flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get into a state' sounds like getting upset; the state is a US one.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, in the west.

clue.text: It's all due to Les! See how he escapes them?

definitions.note: a verb meaning escapes; the rest is surface

explanation.surface: Credit goes to Les for slipping away from his pursuers.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: DUE and LES are mixed with no word saying so; the defining verb is 'escapes'.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to evade or escape from a pursuer, so eludes means escapes.

clue.text: He's unknown to Gran and the rest

explanation.surface: Nobody in the family, Grandma included, knows this man.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: GRAN and REST are mixed with no word saying so.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger is a person one does not know, someone unknown to us.

clue.text: Les is in the hut looking for clues

definitions.note: describes a person: one looking for clues

explanation.surface: Les is searching a shed for evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: A loose old clue: LES and HUT are mixed with no word saying so.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleuth is a detective, a person whose work is hunting for clues.
